title: Read Borrow Pattern
story: Most bugs come from data changing when you don't expect it. The read borrow pattern guarantees your data stays frozen while you inspect it — nobody can modify what you're reading.
why: The read borrow pattern is the most common and safest way to pass data in XIOM — it's zero-cost, prevents accidental mutation, and allows concurrent readers.
analogy: A read borrow is like asking "Can I see that?" — you look at it, you give it back. Nothing changed, and multiple people can look at the same time.
try_it: Add more read-only functions: fn std_dev(scores: &Vec[Int]) -> Float64, fn percentile(scores: &Vec[Int], p: Int) -> Int. All take &, all can coexist.
tips: If your function only reads data, always take & — it's the safest default
Read borrows allow multiple simultaneous readers — no locks needed
The & in the signature tells callers 'this function won't modify your data'
Read borrow functions can call other read borrow functions freely
common_mistakes: Taking owned parameters when & would work — you consume the value unnecessarily
Forgetting to validate with requires — & doesn't validate, it only grants access
Trying to modify data through a & reference — the compiler prevents this
